examples.en: Every morning he douses himself with cold water.
In winter they swim in an ice hole.

related.en: walrus; also a nickname for a winter swimmer

note:
Зака́ливание is hardening the body with cold, air and water.

• зака́ливаться - to harden oneself
• облива́ться холо́дной водо́й - to douse oneself with cold water
• морже́вание - winter swimming in icy water
• про́рубь - a hole cut in the ice for swimming

Морж is both the animal (walrus) and a nickname for a person who swims in the river in winter.

Зака́ливаться should be gradual, and nobody starts морже́вание without seeing a doctor.
title: Hardening and winter swimming: зака́ливание

examples.ru: В сказке [ле́ший] заводит путников в чащу.
examples.en: In the tale, a leshy leads travelers deep into the thicket.
The water spirit lives in a deep pool.

related.en: old woman of the forest, in a hut on chicken legs
an evil old man; his death is hidden in a needle
a simple hero who wins in the end

note:
Russian fairy tales have characters you will not know from English-language tales.

• Ба́ба-Яга́ - an old woman of the forest, in a hut on chicken legs
• Коще́й Бессме́ртный - Koschei the Deathless, an evil old man whose death is hidden in a needle
• ле́ший - a forest spirit, and водяно́й - a water spirit
• Ива́н-дура́к - Ivan the Fool, a simple hero who wins in the end
• богаты́рь - a warrior hero, like Илья́ Му́ромец

Дура́к is otherwise a rude word ('fool'), but in a fairy tale Ivan is likable.
title: Characters of Russian fairy tales

examples.en: I made a tomato salad.
At the store I bought a bunch of lettuce.

related.en: salad (a dish of several ingredients); also lettuce
Olivier salad (Russian salad with potatoes, eggs and mayonnaise)

note:
Сала́т is masculine: вку́сный сала́т.

It means two things:
• a dish of mixed ingredients with mayonnaise or oil: оливье́
• lettuce as a plant: ли́стья сала́та

A cabbage salad is сала́т из капу́сты, a tomato salad - сала́т из помидо́ров.
title: Сала́т is a masculine noun

examples.ru: В субботу мы идём в [го́сти] к бабушке.
examples.en: On Saturday we're going to visit Grandma.

examples.ru: Вчера мы весь вечер были в [гостя́х] у друзей.
examples.en: Yesterday we spent the whole evening at our friends' place.

note:
English says 'go visiting' and 'be visiting'. Russian uses two different cases:

• идти́ в го́сти - to go visiting (куда? - accusative pl.)
• быть в гостя́х - to be visiting (где? - prepositional pl.)

The host is «к» + dative with motion and «у» + genitive with being: идти́ в го́сти к друзья́м, быть в гостя́х у друзе́й.

Russians gladly come with a гости́нец, a small gift such as a cake, fruit or sweets, which goes on the table at once.
title: Visiting: идти́ в го́сти and быть в гостя́х

examples.ru: У нас в доме отключили [горя́чую] воду.
examples.en: The hot water has been turned off in our building.
In summer it's pleasant to swim in warm water.

note:
Hot water from the tap is горя́чая вода́ in Russian. Тёплая means warm or lukewarm.

In Russian cities hot water comes from the city network, so it runs all the time, without a boiler. That is why for 1-3 weeks in summer there is an отключе́ние горя́чей воды́ - yearly maintenance of the network.

• профила́ктика - planned maintenance
• бо́йлер, водонагрева́тель - a device for heating water

On those days people heat water on the stove or use a бо́йлер.
title: Hot water: горя́чая and тёплая

examples.en: Don't address me informally, we don't know each other.
Let's switch to the informal 'you'.

related.en: a toast of brotherhood, a drink to switch to «ты»

note:
If a stranger addresses you as «ты», a Russian may answer sharply:

• Мы с ва́ми детей не крести́ли.
• Мы с ва́ми на брудерша́фт не пи́ли.

Literally: 'we haven't christened children together', 'we haven't drunk to brotherhood'. The meaning: we are not close enough for «ты».

The verbs: ты́кать - to address someone as «ты», вы́кать - as «вы».

The switch to «ты» is agreed on: Дава́йте перейдём на «ты».
title: A warning about «ты»: we haven't drunk to brotherhood

examples.ru: Он [улыбну́лся] из вежливости, но разговаривать не стал.
examples.en: He smiled out of politeness but didn't want to talk.
What are you laughing at? Come on, get to work.

note:
A smile in Russia is not automatically a sign of politeness.

• A Russian may answer a stranger's smile with: Мы знако́мы? - Do we know each other?
• Из ве́жливости улыбну́лся sounds cold: the smile was only formal
• At work or in class a smile for no reason looks unserious
• A sincere smile is valued: if a Russian smiles at you, he means it.

There is even a saying: Смех без причи́ны - при́знак дурачи́ны. That is, someone who laughs for no reason is not quite all there.
title: Laughing for no reason: why Russians smile little

examples.en: Somebody called you, I don't know who.

examples.ru: Если [кто́-нибудь] позвонит, скажи, что я перезвоню.
examples.en: If anyone calls, tell them I'll call back.
I have something for you (but I'm not saying what).

related.en: someone - I know it happened, I don't know who
anyone, someone or other - not sure it will happen
someone - I know who, but I won't say

note:
Where English has 'someone' and 'anyone', Russian has three forms.

• -то: I know something happened, but not who or what (most often the past)
• -нибудь: anyone at all, unspecified - questions, requests, the future: Позвони́ кому́-нибудь.
• кое-: I know, but I'm not telling: Я кое-что́ зна́ю.

The same goes for что, где, куда, когда: куда́-то, когда́-нибудь, кое-где́.
title: Someone and something: -то, -нибудь and кое-

examples.en: Grandma bakes a kulich for Easter.

examples.ru: Мы с детьми [кра́сим] яйца к Пасхе.
examples.en: The kids and I are dyeing eggs for Easter.

related.en: Easter; also a sweet dish made of curd cheese

note:
Easter is Па́сха in Russian.

• кули́ч - an Easter cake; every family has its own recipe
• кра́сить я́йца - to dye eggs; red is the traditional color, but any color will do
• сту́каться я́йцами - to tap eggs against each other
• христо́соваться - to exchange the Easter greeting and kiss three times

The greeting: Христо́с воскре́се! - Вои́стину воскре́се! ('Christ is risen!' - 'Truly He is risen!')

Good Friday (Вели́кая пя́тница) and Easter Monday are not days off.
title: Easter in Russia: Па́сха, кули́ч and христо́соваться

examples.en: The graduates sang songs at the assembly.

examples.ru: Для одиннадцатиклассников [после́дний] звонок прозвенел в мае.
examples.en: For the eleventh-graders the last bell rang in May.

related.en: ceremonial assembly in the school yard

note:
At the end of May Russian schools celebrate the Последний звоно́к.

• лине́йка - a ceremonial assembly in the school yard: speeches, songs, a waltz, balloons
• звоно́к - a first-grader rings a small bell, most often sitting on a graduate's shoulder
• выпускно́й - the graduation party, in June

Where English says 'graduation', Russian separates two things: ЕГЭ is the final exam, and выпускно́й is the celebration.
title: The last bell: how school ends in Russia

examples.ru: Говорят, что покупать вещи до родов - плохая [приме́та].
examples.en: They say it's a bad omen to buy things before the birth.

examples.ru: Не хвали раньше времени, а то [сгла́зишь].
examples.en: Don't boast ahead of time, or you'll jinx it.

related.en: superstition, an omen of luck or bad luck

note:
Russians readily believe in приме́ты.

• Before the birth nothing is bought for the baby, and a pregnant woman does not get a haircut
• сгла́зить means to jinx, so people say тьфу-тьфу-тьфу and постуча́ть по де́реву (knock on wood)
• From the роддо́м (maternity hospital) a woman often goes home for a family lunch, usually with just the closest relatives
title: Omens: superstitions in Russia

examples.en: Please bring me still water.
At the store we always buy mineral water.

note:
In a Russian cafe, water with your coffee is usually not free.

• you order and pay for water: во́да с га́зом or без га́за
• во́да из-под кра́на - tap water; many people do not drink it without a filter or boiling
• кипячёная вода - boiled water

The waiter asks: «С га́зом или без га́за?» - Sparkling or still?
title: Water in a Russian cafe

examples.en: The children are waiting for Ded Moroz and the Snow Maiden.
The presents were lying under the tree.

related.en: the Snow Maiden, Ded Moroz's granddaughter

note:
Дед Моро́з is often called the Russian Santa Claus, but he is a different character.

• tall, with a long beard and a staff, in a long шу́ба (blue, white or red)
• his granddaughter Снегу́рочка (the Snow Maiden) goes with him
• presents are under the fir tree (ёлка), and he comes on New Year's Eve
• he lives in the town of Вели́кий Усты́г

New Year is the main holiday in Russia, and Рождество́ (7 January) is quieter. The greeting: «С Но́вым го́дом!»
title: Дед Моро́з: the Russian Father Frost

examples.ru: Из Москвы я привезла маме красивую [шкату́лку].
examples.en: From Moscow I brought my mother a beautiful lacquer box.
For the winter he bought himself an ushanka.

related.en: matryoshka, a wooden doll within a doll
Gzhel, blue and white painted ceramics

note:
Classic Russian gifts.

• матрёшка - a wooden doll within a doll
• уша́нка - a winter hat with ear flaps
• плато́к - a shawl; the Pavlovo Posad ones (павлопоса́дские) are the most beautiful
• шкату́лка - a small painted box
• гжель - blue and white ceramics
• пастила́, конфе́ты - sweets (конфе́ты are candies, not confetti)
title: What to bring from Russia: souvenirs

examples.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Be so kind, can you tell me what time it is?

related.en: excuse me - the most common way to get someone's attention

note:
Russian has no neutral equivalent of 'sir' and 'madam'.

Суда́рыня and господи́н have gone from everyday speech, and това́рищ and гражда́нка belong to the past. So a stranger is stopped with a formula:
• извини́те
• прости́те
• бу́дьте добры́ - when you are asking for something

The same works for women and men, and the tone decides how polite it sounds.

You also hear де́вушка (young woman) and мужчи́на (man), but some people dislike them, so it is safer to start with извини́те.
title: Addressing a stranger: no 'sir' or 'madam'

examples.en: Thanks for lunch! - You're welcome!
Let's drink to your health!
Achoo! - Bless you!

related.en: you're welcome (said when you have served someone food or drink)

note:
English 'to your health', 'bless you' and 'you're welcome' (after a meal) are three different expressions in Russian:

• на здоро́вье - the answer to спаси́бо when you have treated someone
• за здоро́вье - a toast: За твоё здоро́вье!
• будь здоро́в, бу́дьте здоро́вы - when someone sneezes

The trap: на здоро́вье is not a toast, so do not use it to say cheers.

Other toasts are Ва́ше здоро́вье! and Бу́дем здоро́вы!
title: Cheers, bless you, you're welcome: на здоро́вье, за здоро́вье and будь здоро́в

examples.ru: [Вот] твой ключ, он лежал на столе.
examples.en: Here is your key, it was lying on the table.
Look, there's our train over there!
Well, how about that!

related.en: over there - far away, you are pointing at it

note:
Russian has two words for pointing:

• вот - here is, there it is; the thing is close: Вот твой ключ - Here's your key
• вон - over there; the thing is far away: Вон авто́бус идёт - There goes the bus

Вот is also a particle of emphasis:
• Вот э́то да! - Well, how about that!
• Вот и всё - That's it.
title: Here and there: вот and вон

examples.en: On Epiphany many people swim in an ice hole.
They cut a hole in the ice near the shore.

related.en: a hole cut in the ice for swimming

note:
In Russia Epiphany is usually called Креще́ние, less often Богоявле́ние. The date is 19 January.

The best-known custom is swimming in a про́рубь, a hole in the ice:
1. the person crosses himself
2. plunges in three times
3. this is done in the night of 18-19 January or during the day on the 19th

Priests and doctors warn that it is only for the prepared, and that you should not cut a hole yourself.

People also take свята́я вода́ (holy water) home from church.
title: Epiphany in Russia: Креще́ние and the ice hole

examples.ru: В классе он всегда был [бе́лой воро́ной].
examples.en: In class he was always the odd one out.
In the family they considered him the black sheep.

related.en: a person who differs from the others and does not fit in
a member of the group who brings shame on it
a mangy sheep, a member who ruins the group's reputation

note:
Russian has both images, and they are close to English 'odd one out' and 'black sheep', but the emphasis differs.

• бе́лая воро́на - someone who stands out and does not fit the group; not necessarily an insult
• чёрная овца́ - someone who is a disgrace to the family or group; clearly negative

For a bad member of the group Russian more often says парши́вая овца́: парши́вая овца́ всё ста́до по́ртит (one mangy sheep spoils the whole flock).
title: The white crow and the black sheep

examples.ru: Это были только [цвето́чки], а ягодки ещё впереди.
examples.en: That was only the beginning, and the worst is still ahead.

note:
A Russian expression that sounds like summer but has nothing to do with it:

Э́то ещё цвето́чки, а я́годки впереди́.

Literally: 'these are only little flowers, the berries are ahead'. It means that what is happening now is only the beginning and the real trouble comes later.

• цвето́чки - the first, smaller problems
• я́годки - the real, bigger problems

The expression is used for troubles, not for good things.
title: These are only flowers, the berries are still to come

examples.en: Tea with lemon, please.
Do you want herbal tea?

note:
In Russian, чай without an addition means black or green tea.

• чёрный чай, зелёный чай - ordinary tea
• травяно́й чай - herbal tea, for example with рома́шка (chamomile) or мя́та (mint)
• лека́рственные тра́вы - medicinal herbs; chamomile and mint are more often thought of as these

So in a cafe ask for «чёрный чай» or «зелёный чай».

Tea is usually served with something sweet: пить чай с то́ртом, к ча́ю подаём пече́нье. Чаепи́тие is that whole ritual.
title: Tea in Russia: чай and herbal tea

examples.en: I've been looking for a job for a month.
What are you looking for?

note:
The verb иска́ть has a consonant change in every person, not only in the first:

• я ищу́
• ты и́щешь
• он и́щет
• мы и́щем, вы и́щете
• они́ и́щут

Ск becomes щ. There is no form «я искаю». The past tense is regular: иска́л, иска́ла.

For something specific it takes the accusative: иска́ть рабо́ту. For something abstract it can take the genitive: иска́ть сча́стья.
title: Искать: ищу́, и́щешь

examples.en: The conductor brought us tea in a glass holder.

related.en: faceted glass, a glass with flat sides
a metal glass holder with a handle
train car attendant: checks tickets, serves tea and bedding

note:
On a Russian train tea is traditionally served in a special glass.

• гранёный стака́н - a glass with flat faces
• подстака́нник - a metal holder with a handle into which the glass is put
• проводни́к (проводни́ца) - the car attendant: checks tickets, serves tea and bedding

The подстака́нник is often bought as a souvenir today, and for many people a train ride with one is a symbol of a long journey.
title: A glass in a holder: подстака́нник

examples.ru: В субботу мы идём на [кварти́рник] к друзьям.
examples.en: On Saturday we're going to an apartment concert at some friends' place.

note:
Кварти́рник is an informal concert in someone's apartment: the performer plays or sings in a room or in the kitchen, and the audience sits on chairs and on the floor.

• кварти́ра - an apartment
• кварти́рник - a concert in an apartment

They were popular in the USSR in the 1970s and 1980s and are in fashion again. Russians now organize them outside Russia too.
title: Кварти́рник: a concert in an apartment

examples.ru: Давай сыграем в карты: [коло́да] у меня есть.
examples.en: Let's play cards, I have a deck.

note:
The Russian names of playing cards are not always what you expect.

• коло́да - a deck
• пи́ки - spades
• тре́фы - clubs
• бу́бны - diamonds
• че́рви - hearts
• туз - ace
• коро́ль, да́ма, вале́т - king, queen, jack
title: Playing cards: suits and court cards

examples.en: Children love Cinderella and Snow White.

note:
Many Russian titles are not literal translations of the English ones.

• Руса́лочка - The Little Mermaid
• Зо́лушка - Cinderella
• Белосне́жка и семь гно́мов - Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
• Ле́ди и Бродя́га - Lady and the Tramp
• Спя́щая краса́вица - Sleeping Beauty
• Коро́ль лев - The Lion King

Note: for a mermaid Russians say руса́лка, while сире́на is an alarm or a signal.
title: Disney in Russian: titles of the cartoons

examples.ru: Он [влюби́лся] в неё с первого взгляда.
examples.en: He fell in love with her at first sight.
She has been pining for him for a long time.

note:
To fall in love is влюби́ться, and the action and the state are different:

• я влюби́лась - I fell in love (a moment)
• я влюблена́ - I am in love (a state)

Other words:
• со́хнуть по + dat. - to pine for someone: она́ со́хнет по нему́
• втю́риться в + acc. - colloq., to fall in love, often hard
• потеря́ть го́лову - to lose one's head over love
title: To fall in love: влюби́ться and other words

examples.en: We watched 'Harry Potter' as a family.

note:
In older loanwords, names that begin with the sound h in the original are written in Russian with the letter г.

• Га́млет, Га́рри - Hamlet, Harry
• Ги́тлер, Га́мбург - Hitler, Hamburg
• Голливу́д, Гава́на - Hollywood, Havana
• Голла́ндия - Holland

Newer words have х: хо́бби, ха́кер, Хью́стон, Хемингу́эй.
title: Гарри, Гамлет, Голливуд: «г» in place of «h»

examples.en: We're rooting for the Serbian national team.
He was ill with the flu all week.
I have a headache.

related.en: to be ill; to root for; (3rd pers. боли́т) to hurt

note:
The verb боле́ть means 'to be ill', 'to hurt' and 'to root for'.

• боле́ть чем - to be ill: боле́ть гри́ппом (я боле́ю, ты боле́ешь)
• боле́ть за кого́ - to root for someone: боле́ть за сбо́рную
• боли́т - it hurts: боли́т голова́ (3rd person, second conjugation)

A fan is боле́льщик.

So «я боле́ю» on its own means 'I am ill'; 'I'm rooting' needs за + кого́.
title: To root for: боле́ть за + accusative

examples.en: Today our birthday boy is treating everyone to cake.
The guests congratulated the guest of honor on his sixtieth birthday.

related.en: the person whose birthday it is
the person celebrating a round anniversary

note:
English 'the birthday person' has two Russian names:

• имени́нник - the one whose birthday it is (f. имени́нница)
• юбиля́р - the one celebrating a round year: 50, 60, 70

Имени́ны literally means 'name day', but in conversation it is used for a birthday party.

Russians do not celebrate a 40th birthday, which is a superstition. If they do, they say: «Мне опя́ть три́дцать де́вять» (I'm thirty-nine again).
title: The guest of honor: имени́нник and юбиля́р

examples.ru: В воскресенье мы поедем на [шашлыки́] за город.
examples.en: On Sunday we're driving out of town for a shashlik barbecue.

examples.ru: Отец разжёг [манга́л] и начал жарить мясо.
examples.en: Dad lit the brazier and started grilling the meat.

related.en: shashlik, marinated meat grilled on skewers
a brazier with embers for grilling

note:
A Russian does not go 'for a barbecue' but е́хать на шашлыки́ - always plural, на + accusative.

• шашлы́к - marinated cubes of meat on skewers
• манга́л - a brazier with embers on which the шашлы́к is grilled
• да́ча - a country house, where this often happens

May 1 is now «Пра́здник Весны́ и Труда́» (Spring and Labor Day), and in conversation Первома́й. For many it means a trip to the countryside with шашлыка́ми.
title: Going for shashlik: May Day and the barbecue

examples.en: He is such a normie, he doesn't stand out in any way.

related.en: a girl who seeks men's approval

note:
New words of young people, some of them from English (докс, пи́кми, но́рмис):

• докс - finding and publishing someone's personal data on the internet (doxxing)
• скуф - a man over 30 who lets his appearance go and does not exercise
• пи́кми - a girl who tries hard to please men (pick-me)
• но́рмис - an ordinary person with no standout traits (normie)

This is internet slang: young people understand it, and it does not appear in formal texts.
title: New words of young people: скуф, нормис, пикми, докс

examples.en: Put a pinch of salt into the dough.
Stir in one teaspoon of baking soda.

note:
Measures in Russian recipes are named like this:

• столо́вая ло́жка (ст. л.) - a tablespoon
• ча́йная ло́жка (ч. л.) - a teaspoon
• щепо́тка - a pinch

The verbs are in the infinitive or the imperative: размя́ть ви́лкой, доба́вить, перемеша́ть, замеси́ть те́сто, обжа́рить с двух сторо́н.

When the dough turns golden brown, we say подрумя́нится.
title: A recipe in Russian: spoons and pinches

examples.en: They bought the baby a bright rattle.
Put a bib on the child.

related.en: pacifier; also the rubber nipple of a bottle

note:
A few words for baby gear:

• погрему́шка - a rattle
• слюня́вчик - a bib
• со́ска or пусты́шка - a pacifier
• буты́лочка - a feeding bottle

Со́ска means both a pacifier and the rubber nipple of a bottle, while пусты́шка is only a pacifier.

About an adult, со́ска is vulgar, so it is for babies only.
title: Baby things in Russian

examples.en: Don't cry, it'll heal before the wedding.
The wound healed quickly.

note:
When a child scrapes or bumps something, a Russian says: «До сва́дьбы заживёт!» - it will heal before the wedding, don't worry.

The verb зажи́ть said of a wound means 'to heal': ра́на зажила́ - the wound has healed.

The saying is also told to adults about a small mishap: «Ничего́, до сва́дьбы заживёт!»

The origin is explained in various ways, but none is certain.
title: До сва́дьбы заживёт: comfort for a small injury

examples.ru: Мой дед в семьдесят лет [здоро́в] как бык.
examples.en: My grandfather is as healthy as a bull at seventy.

examples.ru: Не обращай внимания, он сегодня [зол] как собака.
examples.en: Don't mind him, he's furious today.

note:
Russian likes short similes: adjective + как + noun.

• дово́лен как слон - very pleased
• зол как соба́ка - furious, angry as a dog
• трусли́в как за́яц - timid as a hare
• наду́лся как индю́к - sulking, puffed up like a turkey
• здоро́в как бык - strong and healthy
• спит как суро́к - sleeps soundly

These expressions usually have the short form of the adjective: здоро́в, зол, дово́лен.
title: Comparisons with animals: здоро́в как бык

examples.en: He grew up in a communal apartment in St Petersburg.
Every month we pay the utility bills.

note:
The word коммуна́лка has two meanings.

• коммуна́льная кварти́ра - a communal apartment: each family has one room, and the kitchen, bathroom and hallway are shared
• платить за коммуна́лку - to pay the utility bills

Communal apartments appeared after 1917, when large apartments were divided into rooms. People lived in them for decades, and a few still exist today, mostly in St Petersburg.

Utilities are коммуна́льные услу́ги, and a neighbor from such an apartment is a сосе́д по коммуна́лке.
title: Utility bills and the коммуна́лка

examples.ru: Я часто [ловлю́] себя на том, что говорю сам с собой.
examples.en: I often catch myself talking to myself.

examples.ru: Вчера я [пойма́л] себя на мысли, что скучаю по зиме.
examples.en: Yesterday I caught myself thinking that I miss the winter.

note:
To notice something about yourself, Russian 'catches' you.

• Ловлю́ себя́ на том, что улыба́юсь. - I catch myself smiling.
• Я пойма́л себя́ на мы́сли, что хочу́ домо́й. - I caught myself thinking I want to go home.

The structure is always the same:
1. лови́ть (imperfective) or пойма́ть (perfective)
2. себя́ in the accusative
3. на том, что or на мы́сли, что and a new clause

There is no infinitive: на том takes что and a full clause.
title: Noticing something about yourself: ловить себя на том, что

examples.en: Don't stand on the threshold, come in.
Nothing is passed across the threshold.

note:
In an old Russian belief the threshold (поро́г) is the border between your world and someone else's, and the ancestors live beneath it.

• nothing is passed across the threshold, and people do not shake hands or greet each other across it: it leads to a quarrel
• you do not stand on the threshold: come in or go out

The saying: через поро́г не здоро́вываются, не передаю́т. Many Russians still do so today, though sometimes they joke about it.
title: The threshold: why nothing is passed across it

examples.en: Pasha is working from home today.
Kolya promised to call this evening.

note:
In everyday speech Russians use short forms of names, and the full name is for documents and a formal tone.

• Ива́н - Ва́ня
• Никола́й - Ко́ля
• Па́вел - Па́ша
• Константи́н - Ко́стя
• Ви́ктор - Ви́тя
• Влади́мир - Во́ва, Воло́дя
• Вячесла́в - Сла́ва

These are not diminutives for children: grown men are called this way at work and among friends.
title: Names in conversation: Ва́ня, Ко́ля, Па́ша

examples.en: Hand me the tape, please, the box has come open.
I need to make a photocopy of my passport.

note:
In Russian some brand names have become the name for all similar things.

• скотч - adhesive tape (and Scotch whisky)
• ксе́рокс - a photocopy: сде́лать ксе́рокс
• па́мперс - any disposable diaper, officially подгу́зник
• джип - any SUV, officially внедоро́жник

A флома́стер is a thin felt-tip pen, a ма́ркер is a thicker one.
title: Brand names that became ordinary words

examples.en: Don't cry, hang in there, Cossack, and you'll be a chief someday!

examples.ru: Он долго [терпе́л] боль и не жаловался.
examples.en: He endured the pain for a long time and did not complain.

note:
Терпи́, каза́к, атама́ном бу́дешь means 'hang in there, Cossack, and you will be a chief'. It is known from Gogol's «Тарас Бульба».

It comforts someone who is having a hard time and reminds them that a big goal sometimes demands putting up with discomfort. Parents often say it to children as a joke, for example before a blood test.

It is close in spirit to 'no pain, no gain'.
title: A saying from Taras Bulba: hang in there and you'll be a chief

examples.en: Tomorrow is a holiday, we're not working.

note:
The main holidays and dates:

• Но́вый год - 1 January
• Рождество́ - 7 January (Orthodox Christmas)
• День защи́тника Оте́чества - 23 February (Defender of the Fatherland Day)
• 8 Ма́рта - Women's Day, when flowers are given
• Пра́здник Весны́ и Труда́ - 1 May (Spring and Labor Day)
• День Побе́ды - 9 May (Victory Day)
• День Росси́и - 12 June (Russia Day)
• День наро́дного еди́нства - 4 November (National Unity Day)
title: Public holidays in Russia

note:
In Russian messages a smile is usually just a bracket, without the colon.

• ) - a smile
• ))) - laughter: the more brackets, the bigger the laugh
• ( - sadness

To an English speaker ")))" may look like a typo. Russians put it in almost every friendly message, and a message without it can seem cold.
title: Russian smileys: ))) instead of :)
